item.title: Mission Harmony 2026: Chinese naval hospital ship visits Côte d'Ivoire
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
ABIDJAN, Côte d'Ivoire , Oct. 15 -- The Chinese naval hospital ship Auspicious Ark, which is carrying out Mission Harmony 2026, arrived at Port of Abidjan in Côte d'Ivoire on October 14, for a seven day goodwill visit. This marks the first visit by a Chinese naval hospital ship to Côte d'Ivoire. During the visit, the mission commander will hold discussions and exchanges with senior Ivorian military and political officials. Leveraging its main platform, the hospital ship will provide medical services to the local patients. It will also dispatch a medical exchange team and a mobile medical team to carry out medical exchanges and outreach consultations at Abidjan Military Hospital and Félix Houphouët Boigny University. In addition, a deck reception will be hosted to strengthen friendship and mutual trust between the two sides.

item.title: Xi's article on advancing Party self-governance to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance with higher standards and more concrete measures, will be published on Friday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 20th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. It calls for upholding and strengthening overall Party leadership and persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance to turn the blueprint drawn up at the fourth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee into reality. It stresses that the Party Central Committee's major policy decisions and arrangements must be implemented with stronger determination and vigor. It also demands strengthening concrete, targeted and regular oversight of the implementation of strategic initiatives, such as applying the new development philosophy, promoting high-quality development, and accelerating the building of a new development paradigm. The article requires more scientific and effective efforts to confine power to an institutional cage. It highlights that everyone is equal before laws and regulations, with no exemptions or special privileges when observing and enforcing these rules. The article says that the fight against corruption must be pursued with greater sobriety and resolve. It describes the anti-corruption campaign as a high-stakes struggle that cannot be lost, requiring an unswerving high-pressure posture to be maintained. It further demands the timely detection, accurate identification and effective resolution of all forms of corruption, with refined anti-corruption mechanisms that align oversight actions across all sectors.

item.title: China urges Japan's incumbent leadership to face history, break with militarist past after latest Yasukuni records revealed
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
China on Thursday urged Japan's incumbent leadership to face up to history, reflect on their country's wartime crimes and make a clean break with militarism after Japanese media reports disclosed, for the first time, internal meeting records from Yasukuni Shrine that systematically document the decision-making process behind the enshrinement of 14 Class-A war criminals, including Hideki Tojo. According to the records, the Japanese government reached an arrangement with the shrine on their enshrinement as early as the 1960s but kept it from the public. The relevant facts did not come to light until 1979. In response to a question regarding the matter, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a press briefing that the relevant records serve as fresh proof that Japan was fully aware that enshrining Class A war criminals was disgraceful and felt guilty about it. It acted with deliberate scheming and colluded tacitly throughout the decision-making process. These Class A war criminals were the chief culprits of Japan's militarist wars of aggression, with their hands stained with the blood of people in victimized countries, Mao said. "The solemn rulings of the Tokyo Trials nailed these war criminals to the pillar of shame in human history, upheld international justice, and laid the legal foundation for the post war international order. How can Japan's incumbent leaders, who repeatedly pay homage to this de facto 'war criminal shrine,' have any sense of conscience?" said Mao. History brooks no distortion, and truth cannot be erased. The crimes committed by Japanese militarism during its wars of aggression are supported by irrefutable evidence. Japan's leaders should face up to history, reflect on those crimes and make a clean break with militarism, said Mao.

item.title: Ode to the Long March | The Road Knows
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
It was the arduous and perilous expedition that forged the great Long March spirit. Back then, some "Little Red Army Soldiers" also embarked on the hard journey. Following the Red Army ranks, they crossed snow-capped mountains and trekked across boundless grasslands, overcoming severe hardships and countless life-or-death trials. Going through the flames of war, they finally grew into resolute and faithful Red Army fighters with indomitable courage and will of steel. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Let us follow the footsteps of those young Red Army soldiers and look back on their legendary stories. item.title: Xi meets Togo's president of Council of Ministers, elevating bilateral ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé in Beijing on Tuesday, during which the two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era. Xi pointed out that the traditional China-Togo friendship was personally forged by leaders of an older generation of both countries, enjoying a solid foundation and growing ever stronger with the passage of time. China and Togo share aligned visions for friendly cooperation and enjoy broad prospects ahead, Xi said. Xi called on the two sides to further enhance exchanges at all levels between the two parties and the two countries, deepen the sharing of experiences in governance, and firmly support each other on issues concerning core interests and major concerns. China welcomes Togo to effectively utilize measures such as China's zero-tariff policy and the "green channel" for products exported to China, further enhance its role as a regional hub for trade and logistics, and facilitate the entry of more distinctive local and regional products into the Chinese market, Xi added. Xi noted that China appreciates Togo's efforts to expand the cross-border use of the RMB and is willing to strengthen cooperation with Togo in new energy, digital intelligence and other fields to support Togo's industrialization process. Noting that China and Togo share similar positions on international and regional affairs, Xi also called on the two sides to enhance multilateral coordination. Xi put forward four principles for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa. First, adhering to the principle of "Africa-led." The African people are the true masters of Africa and should play a central role in regional affairs, Xi said. Second, upholding fairness and justice. All participating parties should abide by the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned, he noted. Third, promoting ceasing hostilities for peace. Wars and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve conflicts between countries. It is imperative to uphold mutual respect, conduct extensive consultations, seek common ground while shelving differences, and practice mutual understanding and accommodation. Fourth, addressing both symptoms and root causes. Efforts should focus on immediate security while planning for long-term development, Xi said. Faure, who is on an official visit to China, said that during his visit, he personally witnessed the remarkable achievements of Chinese modernization and the extensive promotion of fine traditional Chinese culture under the leadership of President Xi, and gained a deeper understanding of China's governance philosophy and the key to success. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, he said Togo is willing to enhance mutual trust with China, strengthen dialogue and communication, deepen enduring and mutually beneficial cooperation to jointly build a Togo-China community with a shared future for the new era, and better benefit the two peoples. The Togolese side fully agrees with the important principles proposed by President Xi for the constructive participation of all parties in the settlement of hotspot issues in Africa, Faure said. He expressed Togolese appreciation for China on its significant role in maintaining world peace and stability and jointly addressing global challenges, as well as the willingness to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China, jointly uphold multilateralism, and safeguard the interests of developing countries. item.title: Chinese mainland blasts Taiwan authorities' separatist rhetoric regarding history
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
BEIJING, Oct. 14 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities in Taiwan, saying they had unscrupulously distorted history and hyped separatist rhetoric based on a warped version of history. Such rhetoric on history revealed the DPP authorities' true intention of inciting cross-Strait confrontation, said Chen Binhua, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, when responding to a media question on Taiwan authorities' and Lai Ching-te's remarks regarding the history of World War II. It also showed the DPP authorities' ignorance of history and betrayal of the ancestors, Chen said. The Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression was the first to break out and lasted the longest in the World Anti-Fascist War, or World War II, resulting in over 35 million Chinese military and civilian casualties from 1931 to 1945. The victory of the war and the recovery of Taiwan from Japanese occupation are great victories achieved by the Chinese people, including those in Taiwan, at the cost of blood and lives, Chen noted. Taiwan's liberation from the shackles of Japan's colonial rule and its return to the motherland represent an important outcome of the Chinese people's victory in fighting Japanese aggressors, and form an integral part of the post-World War II international order, Chen said. It's a historical memory the Chinese people across the Taiwan Strait should never forget, said Chen, urging compatriots in Taiwan to see the true face of the DPP authorities and stand on the right side of history. Following the Chinese people's victory in the war of resistance against Japanese aggressors, a full-blown civil war broke out between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT). In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. This unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, but the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. The real status quo across the Taiwan Strait is that there is only one China in the world and that Taiwan is a part of China, Chen said. By promoting a false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism," stoking cross-Strait confrontation, or attempting to pursue "Taiwan independence" through military means and by relying on foreign forces, the DPP authorities will only gradually drag Taiwan into a dangerous situation and bring great disaster to the people in Taiwan, Chen noted.

item.title: Ode to the Long March | The Lamp Glows
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
This is a real story in the Long March. In October 1934, a mother who had ten sons sent eight of her sons to join the Red Army on the Long March. From then on, the mother lit a kerosene lamp every night, waiting for her sons to return. The camphor tree at the village entrance witnessed her 26 years of waiting until she passed away. She never saw her sons again, but she witnessed the founding of New China that her sons had fought for. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Let us go back to the side of that camphor tree and recall the legendary story.
